techniques.name: York County town pages
techniques.hypothesis: 'gutter installation <town> pa' has buying intent, low competition, and almost no local contractor has a real page for it. One well-written town page a day builds a moat across the county that a competitor would have to spend months matching.
techniques.evidence: The five existing area pages are the site's only town-level coverage; York County has 70+ municipalities.

techniques.name: Cost and buying guides
techniques.hypothesis: Cost queries are the highest-intent traffic a contractor can get, and most contractors refuse to discuss price — which is why Angi and HomeAdvisor outrank them and then sell the lead back. Answering the price question honestly should win the click and the call.
techniques.evidence: Uncovered price-intent queries in the tracked universe.

techniques.name: Area-page link mesh
techniques.hypothesis: New town pages are orphans until something links to them. A nearby-areas mesh gets them crawled in days instead of weeks and passes local relevance between them.
techniques.evidence: Standard internal-linking practice; costs nothing to run.

techniques.name: LocalBusiness structured data
techniques.hypothesis: The map pack is where the money queries are actually won. Consistent name/address/phone in structured data on the site is the part of that Eric controls directly.
techniques.evidence: NAP consistency is a documented local-pack ranking factor.

techniques.name: Sitemap refresh
techniques.hypothesis: New pages are not crawled until they are in the sitemap.
techniques.evidence: Existing seo/gen_sitemap.py, re-run after each build.

techniques.name: Same-morning IndexNow push
techniques.hypothesis: Submitting only the URLs written this morning gets them into Bing and Copilot within minutes rather than waiting for the 03:05 full-sitemap run the following day.
techniques.evidence: IndexNow is supported by Bing, Yandex, Seznam and Naver.

techniques.name: Ask finished jobs for a Google review
techniques.hypothesis: Review count and recency are the strongest lever on map-pack rank for a service business. The profile sits at 13 reviews; competitors ranking above it have dozens. Every completed booking in the database is a customer who was never asked.
techniques.evidence: Google's own local-ranking guidance names review count and score.
techniques.notes: first step: confirm with Eric that customers may be emailed a review request after a completed job, then flip this to active. It emails real customers, so it stays off until a human says yes.

techniques.name: Weekly Business Profile posts
techniques.hypothesis: Business Profile posts keep the listing active and surface seasonal offers directly in the pack, where the hire-intent searches land.
techniques.evidence: GBP is live with ~300 monthly views and 4.2 stars.
techniques.notes: first step: OAuth access to the Business Profile API for enemo@nemoseamlessgutter.com — the engine cannot post without it.

techniques.name: NAP citations on local directories
techniques.hypothesis: Consistent citations across the directories Google cross-checks raise local-pack confidence, and several of them rank for the money queries themselves.
techniques.evidence: Standard local-SEO practice; NAP already verified consistent on-site.
techniques.notes: first step: most directories need a captcha or a phone verification, so this produces a submission pack for Eric rather than auto-submitting. Flip to active once the pack format is agreed.

techniques.name: Connect Search Console
techniques.hypothesis: The >50% top-3 goal is not measurable without Search Console. Until it is connected the engine reports coverage as a proxy and cannot tell whether it is actually winning.
techniques.evidence: seo/weekly_digest.py already contains a working GSC client.
techniques.notes: first step: create a Google Cloud service account, grant it read access to the nemoseamlessgutter.com Search Console property, and drop the JSON at seo/gsc-service-account.json (chmod 600).

techniques.name: Google Local Services Ads (Google Verified badge)
techniques.hypothesis: LSAs sit above the map pack and organic results for 'gutter installer near me york pa' type searches, and you only pay when someone actually calls or messages — which puts NEMO's phone above every organic and directory listing exactly when a York County homeowner has an urgent leak or is ready to book, without needing an ad agency or five-figure PPC budget.
techniques.evidence: Google Local Service Ads (LSAs) put your business at the very top of search results — above regular Google Ads, above the map pack, above everything — and you only pay when a real customer calls or messages. <cite index="26-3,26-5">Google Local Service Ads (LSAs) put your business at the very top of search results — above regular Google Ads, above the map pack, above everything — and you only pay when a real customer calls or messages. The pay-per-lead model is intact and still works: home-service contractors pay roughly $25–$80 per lead on average.</cite> Adoption among contractors is already high: <cite index="34-7">Adoption has climbed from roughly 28% of contractors using LSA in 2022 to an estimated 70% by late 2025.</cite> https://pushleads.com/google-local-service-ads-verified-badge-2026/ and https://pipelineon.com/blog/google-local-service-ads-for-contractors/
techniques.notes:
first step: Apply for Google Local Services in the Google Ads dashboard, submit Eric's license, insurance, and pass the background check to get the blue Google Verified badge, then set a conservative weekly budget cap
effort: days
cost: more
expected: 5-15 verified phone/message leads per month at a controlled weekly budget (start ~$150-250/wk cap), booking 30-40% of them per industry benchmarks

techniques.name: Claim Nextdoor Business Page + ask finished jobs for a neighbor recommendation
techniques.hypothesis: York County neighborhoods (especially older/historic districts where half-round and copper gutters matter) run heavily on Nextdoor word-of-mouth; a free, verified Business Page collecting real recommendations from actual customers turns each finished job into visible proof for everyone in that neighborhood who searches 'gutter' or asks for a recommendation, at zero cost and with no review-gating risk since Nextdoor recommendations are a separate, opt-in feature from Google reviews.
techniques.evidence: Nextdoor is explicitly built around word-of-mouth trust: <cite index="19-1,19-2">People want to work with businesses that their neighbors work with and trust. Nextdoor provides a platform to facilitate that.</cite> Recommendations compound visibility — <cite index="20-8">Business Pages with recommendations have up to 19X the page views compared to pages without.</cite> Nextdoor also suggests a simple, honest way to gather them: <cite index="20-10">Share your Business Page link with customers after each job or transaction and ask them to leave you a recommendation.</cite> https://business.nextdoor.com/en-us/blog/nextdoor-insights-neighbors-value-recommendations
techniques.notes:
first step: Claim and verify the free NEMO Nextdoor Business Page with current NAP, then text/email the next 5 completed customers the Business Page link asking for an honest recommendation
effort: hours
cost: free
expected: Business Page claimed and verified within a week; 5-10 organic recommendations within 60 days; measurable referral calls citing 'saw you on Nextdoor'

techniques.name: 5-minute human callback on every AI-phone-agent lead
techniques.hypothesis: The AI phone agent already captures leads while Eric is on a roof, but capturing isn't the same as closing — the booking rate collapses if the human follow-up call slips past the first few minutes, and this business's entire measured problem right now is 0 bookings/leads yesterday against 2 all-time bookings, meaning conversion of captured leads into estimates is the real bottleneck, not traffic.
techniques.evidence: Response speed is decisive for home-service calls: <cite index="6-16">The MIT and InsideSales lead-response study found you are 100 times more likely to reach a web lead and 21 times more likely to qualify it when you respond within 5 minutes versus 30.</cite> Contractors who win leads treat this as the whole game: <cite index="33-6,33-7">The contractors who still get quality leads have figured out screening. They return calls within 5 minutes (first call back wins).</cite> And the cost of not doing it is real: <cite index="9-14,9-15,9-16">85% never call back. 62% contact a competitor immediately. 78% of deals go to the first business that responds.</cite>
techniques.notes:
first step: Set a phone alert/checklist so Eric checks the AI phone agent's lead log every time he steps off a roof or between jobs, and calls back every captured lead within 5 minutes, logging the callback time against each lead
effort: hours
cost: free
expected: Callback-within-5-minutes rate goes from unmeasured to tracked and >90%; lead-to-booked-estimate conversion rate rises measurably from its current near-zero baseline

last_scout.notes: Rejected: shared-lead marketplaces (Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack) — they sell the same lead to multiple contractors and push price competition, which conflicts with the 'exclusive, honest, phone-ringing-here' goal; a small agency retainer or Google/Facebook display ad buy — too costly and not owner-executable without a marketing department; buying backlinks or citation packages beyond honest directory listings — against the no-bought-links rule already noted in the ledger. LSA cost is variable and should be budget-capped weekly so it never becomes a five-figure spend; treat the first 30 days as a test at the low end of the budget range. Nextdoor recommendations must never be incentivized or gated — only ask, never offer anything in exchange, to stay compliant and honest. The speed-to-lead technique costs nothing but requires Eric's discipline; if AI-agent lead volume grows enough that it interferes with roof work, revisit whether a low-cost answering/dispatch helper is worth it later.
